scope: EU member states and other jurisdictions applying the EU type-approval framework
access: Reported to authorities; no centralized public incident-level feed identified
notes: Manufacturers of covered fully automated vehicles must report safety-critical occurrences and periodic in-service monitoring information to type-approval/market-surveillance authorities and the European Commission.

scope: UK self-driving pilots and the Automated Vehicles Act framework
access: Mandatory reporting to UK authorities; public incident-level publication remains limited
notes: UK pilot guidance requires operators to report safety-relevant occurrences, including collisions and traffic infractions. This creates a separate official reporting pathway for the UK after Brexit.

access: Varies by country; may include public datasets, project reports, regulator releases or records-access requests
notes: Examples include Sweden's STRADA, Norway's Statens vegvesen AV-testing permits and experience reports, Swiss FEDRO/cantonal records, and national type-approval authorities. These can corroborate or uncover crashes not visible in media searches.

scope: EU road crashes involving death or injury
notes: Useful as a backstop for injury/fatal crashes, but standard public CARE fields do not directly identify ADS engagement, so matching requires external incident details.

scope: Publicly reported automated-driving crashes across Europe
notes: Primary beta discovery layer. Multiple reports about one real-world event are merged into one canonical incident. Operator, police and public-agency statements are preferred when available.
